chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Aba al-Yasa', from Aba al-Jarud, from Aba Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Abandon speculating about Allah, for indeed speculating about Allah does not increase except in bewilderment, because Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, cannot be perceived by the eyes, nor can the reports/reachings of the mind reach Him.
ai.seo_question: Why does Imam al-Baqir advise against speculating about Allah's essence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) warns against excessive speculative theology (tafwit) regarding Allah's essence, noting that it leads to spiritual arrogance or bewilderment rather than true knowledge. This teaching underscores the Shia principle of divine transcendence (tanzih), where human intellect is limited to recognizing attributes rather than comprehending the essence, as neither physical sight nor intellectual 'reports' can fully encompass the Divine. This hadith serves as a critical boundary for theological discourse, preventing the projection of human limitations onto the Infinite.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 13. And with the same chain of transmission, on the authority of Abut al-Yas`, on the authority of Abu al-Jarud that Abu Ja`far al-Baqir (AS) said: “
Abandon speculating about Allah. Verily, speculating about Allah does nothing but lead astray. Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, cannot be perceived by vision, and the reports cannot reach Him.”
